title: Ginkgo: Ancient Ginkgo Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: The species that outlived the dinosaurs and survived Hiroshima. The oldest ginkgos mapped so far, from Tokyo shrine giants to Europe's first imports.
intro: The ginkgo has no living relatives. Its family goes back over 200 million years, so far that when the first botanists examined one they were looking at a tree older than flowers; everything else in its lineage is fossil. It nearly vanished too, surviving in Chinese temple grounds until monks and then Dutch traders carried it around the world. It is almost comically hard to kill: six ginkgos stood within two kilometres of the Hiroshima blast and all six leafed the following spring. Cities love it for that same stubbornness, and every November it pays them back, dropping all its golden fan-shaped leaves at once, sometimes in a single day. The ginkgos mapped so far run from Tokyo's shrine giants to the first European imports, oldest first.
